question: Should OpenRouter music generation fail closed at the proposed 2 MiB pending SSE, 64 MiB decoded audio, and 1 MiB transcript limits, or should those thresholds be changed before merge?
rationale: The implementation is narrow and well placed, but the exact thresholds can reject large outputs that current releases attempted to buffer, so automation should not choose that compatibility boundary alone.

options.title: Accept Current Caps
options.body: Merge the provider-local caps as a deliberate memory-safety boundary and treat over-limit outputs as deterministic provider failures.

options.title: Adjust Thresholds First
options.body: Ask for a narrow commit raising, documenting, or otherwise tuning the caps if maintainers expect larger legitimate OpenRouter music outputs.

options.title: Defer For Shared Media Policy
options.body: Pause the PR if OpenClaw should standardize generated-media output caps across providers before adding OpenRouter-specific limits.

recommendation.title: Accept Current Caps
recommendation.body: Merge the provider-local caps as a deliberate memory-safety boundary and treat over-limit outputs as deterministic provider failures.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete introduced the OpenRouter music-generation provider and has the strongest history signal for accepting its provider behavior contract.
